objects.abstract: SCOPE CORRECTION — read before any other object in this bundle
objects.content: Corrected 2026-07-28 after re-running every script in the TuringStack repository. This bundle does NOT describe a demonstrated break of any deployed cryptographic primitive. It describes: (1) an exact algebraic theorem over Cayley-Dickson algebras mod 2; (2) an exact, reproducible structural observation about SHA-1's constants; (3) a retrospective reading of the ALREADY-PUBLIC SHA-1 collision (SHAttered, 2017); and (4) an ECC threat MODEL whose exploit step is explicitly an OPEN PROBLEM. No private-key recovery, signature forgery, or SHA-2/SHA-3 attack is demonstrated. A prior version of this bundle's metadata assigned CVSS 7.5 and listed secp256k1/OpenSSL/Bitcoin/Ethereum as affected and filed to CISA/NIST/MITRE/CERT-CC; those claims are RETRACTED as unsupported by the code. They are recorded in note--disclosure-metadata for the record, not asserted.

objects.name: Cayley-Dickson-over-GF(2) zero-divisor structure: a research framework and ECC threat model (exploit OPEN, not demonstrated)
objects.description: ESTABLISHED THEOREM: for any n=2^k, every element x of the Cayley-Dickson algebra T_n over GF(2) satisfies x^2 in {0, e_0}; equivalently the trace-Laplacian Delta(w)=w*(0xFF..F) is zero iff w is nilpotent iff w lies on the zero-divisor nodal line. Exact, checked directly. STRUCTURAL OBSERVATIONS (exact, reproducible): all five SHA-1 IV constants (H0-H4) are nilpotent in T32 and lie on the nodal line at spectral distance 0, while the four round constants (K0-K3) sit at the maximum distance 32 (bimodal split); secp256k1's generator coordinates Gx, Gy are both involutory (x^2=e_0) in T256/GF(2). RETROSPECTIVE: the known SHA-1 collision can be read as a T32 zero-divisor event. OPEN / NOT DEMONSTRATED: polynomial-time navigation to the locus; ECC secp256k1 key recovery (carry-closing mod p is the sole barrier and its complexity is an OPEN PROBLEM); RSA/ECDSA recovery (measured at chance in this project); any SHA-2/SHA-3 attack. NULL: a sedenion factoring-locality test returned no signal (random pairs matched or exceeded factor pairs; a reported 'ratio=inf' was a 0/0 divide-by-zero artifact). No working exploit is provided or implied.

external_references.description: Stevens, Bursztein, Karpman, Albertini, Markov — first SHA-1 collision, 2017 (the already-public result this framework reads retrospectively)

objects.content:
1) T_n/GF(2) trace-Laplacian theorem: Delta(w)=0 iff w nilpotent. Exact.
2) SHA-1 IVs nilpotent in T32 (all on nodal line, distance 0): H0=0x67452301, H1=0xEFCDAB89, H2=0x98BADCFE, H3=0x10325476, H4=0xC3D2E1F0. Round constants K0-K3 at maximum distance 32. Reproduced 2026-07-28.
3) secp256k1 generator: Gx and Gy both involutory (x^2=e_0) in T256/GF(2); Gx*Gy != 0.
These are structural facts. None constitutes an attack on a deployed primitive; see the vulnerability object's OPEN/NULL findings.

objects.name: Guidance (precautionary / research-directed — NOT incident response)
objects.description: No deployed system is shown to require remediation by this work. Precautionary and research-directed only: (research) close or bound the OPEN problem of polynomial-time navigation to the zero-divisor locus before any operational claim; (research) sedenion/CD-aware structural analysis as one input to future curve and hash constant selection. Post-quantum migration (ML-KEM, ML-DSA, SLH-DSA) is sound practice on its own merits and is UNRELATED to any result here. CRYSTALS-Kyber, Dilithium, FALCON, SPHINCS+ are not assessed and not implicated.
